standard_prerequisites.name: Profiles of matchings in the hypercube Q^n
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a matching M in the cube Q^n the profile is the vector x in N^n whose i-th coordinate counts the edges of M whose endpoints differ in the i-th coordinate; a tuple is admissible when it is the profile of some matching, even when every coordinate is even, and perfect when the sum of the coordinates equals 2^{n-1}; the article's own definitions are retained at source line 51.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the meaning of admissible, even and perfect for the counted lemma, whose conclusion asserts the existence of a perfect even tuple in N^n.

standard_prerequisites.name: Precedence order on tuples and down-closedness of admissible tuples
standard_prerequisites.statement: For x and z in N^n the article writes z precedes x, in symbols z <= x, when z_i <= x_i for every i; the set of admissible tuples is down-closed in this partial order, and (x,z) denotes the concatenation of x in N^n and z in N^m as a vector in N^{n+m}; retained at source line 64.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma concludes y <= y' for a suitable perfect even y' in N^n, which is exactly this order; the down-closedness is why a perfect even tuple dominating y transfers admissibility to y.

standard_prerequisites.name: The parity obstruction of Balister, Gyori and Schelp
standard_prerequisites.statement: If the cube F_2^n is partitioned into pairs {a_i,b_i} with differences d_i, then the sum of all d_i vanishes, because each vertex occurs exactly once on each side of the sum; the article records this identity at source lines 30-33 and the conjecture that it is also sufficient at source lines 34-36.
standard_prerequisites.use: Background for the evenness condition that the counted lemma assumes on its input tuple x in N^{n+1}.

core_obligations: Read off the hypotheses of the counted lemma: n >= 2, the tuple x in N^{n+1} is even, ||x||_1 <= 2^n, and the last coordinate satisfies x_{n+1} >= 2 o(x) for the count o(x) of the non-final coordinates congruent to 2 modulo 4.
Form the halved tuple y = (x_1/2, ..., x_n/2) and the 0-1 indicator vector o whose i-th entry is 1 exactly when x_i is congruent to 2 modulo 4, so that ||o||_1 = o(x) (source lines 158-162).
Set z = y + o and verify both that y <= z and that z is even, using the defining property of the indicator vector (source line 163).
Estimate ||z||_1 <= sum_i (x_i/2 + o_i) <= ||x||_1 / 2 <= 2^{n-1}, where the middle inequality uses ||o||_1 = o(x) <= x_{n+1}/2 and the last one uses ||x||_1 <= 2^n (source lines 165-168).

Conclude that a perfect even y' in N^n with y' >= z >= y exists, because 2^{n-1} is even and a tuple of norm at most 2^{n-1} can be enlarged coordinatewise to norm exactly 2^{n-1} while staying even (source line 169).

proof_roadmap.step: State the lemma: for even x in N^{n+1} with ||x||_1 <= 2^n and x_{n+1} >= 2 o(x), the halved tuple y is dominated by some perfect even tuple y'.
Define the indicator o_i of the congruence x_i = 2 mod 4 and collect the count ||o||_1 = o(x) <= x_{n+1}/2.
Put z = y + o; then y <= z and z is even.
Enlarge z coordinatewise to a perfect even tuple y' >= z, which is dominated by no admissible obstruction.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2404.03950v3 的 Lemma l:first（源 154-156 行，紧接的作者证明 157-170 行）：给定偶数元组 x 属于 N^{n+1}，满足 ||x||_1 <= 2^n 且末坐标 x_{n+1} >= 2 o(x)，其中 o(x) 数出除末位外模 4 余 2 的坐标个数，要证明减半元组 y=(x_1/2,...,x_n/2) 被某个完美偶数元组 y' 支配。关键操作有两处不是例行核验：一是必须把「哪些坐标会破坏 y 的偶数性」精确地编码成 0-1 指示向量 o（158-162 行），从而 z=y+o 既支配 y 又是偶数；二是要把充分性条件 x_{n+1} >= 2 o(x) 转成范数估计 ||z||_1 <= ||x||_1/2 <= 2^{n-1}（165-168 行），再由 2^{n-1} 为偶数把 z 逐坐标放大到恰好范数 2^{n-1} 的完美偶数元组（169 行）。难点在于「放大到恰好 2^{n-1}」这一步要求放大后仍为偶数，而 z 已经是偶数且其范数至多 2^{n-1}，这需要同时用到偶数性与整数性；这一引理正是该文归纳证明的枢纽（原文 146-150 行说明其用途），并由它把主定理化归为有限个基例。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Lemma l:first at source lines 154-156 together with the proof environment that begins on the next line (157-170); the pairing is the ordinary adjacent one and the proof ends before the author's proof of Theorem t:perfect opens at source line 172.

The retained context at source lines 30-36 and 51 is the article's own statement of the Balister-Gyori-Schelp necessary condition and conjecture and the article's own definitions of profile, admissible, even and perfect tuples.

The retained context at source line 64 is the article's own definition of the precedence order and of the concatenation of tuples; it is retained because the counted lemma concludes y <= y' and because the down-closedness of admissible tuples stated there is what makes the dominating tuple useful.
The retained context at source line 152 is the article's own definition of the quantity o(x); it is retained because the hypothesis x_{n+1} >= 2 o(x) of the counted lemma is stated in terms of it.

The native preamble is retained from source lines 2-18, that is the article class, geometry, AMS, bm, mathtools, comment, enumerate and tikz packages and the author's theorem declarations; the title and author lines at source lines 19-20 are not part of the preamble fragment and the document body is not retained.

No retained line contains a citation, so the material carries no bibliography; the retained lines refer only to the label c:BGS, which the retained conjecture at source lines 34-36 defines, and to the label t:perfect, which is left undefined by the retained fragments and is therefore declared as a non-load-bearing navigation pointer rather than as a premise.
